    AI Overview
    Only three golfers in history have won back-to-back Masters tournaments, successfully defending their title at Augusta National: Jack Nicklaus (1965–1966), Nick Faldo (1989–1990), and Tiger Woods (2001–2002). No golfer has won three consecutive Masters tournaments. 
    This video shows a brief history of the Masters tournament, including some of the back-to-back winners:
    1m
    The 90th Masters Tournament
    The Masters
    YouTube• Apr 6, 2026
    Jack Nicklaus (1965–1966): The first to achieve this feat, winning by nine strokes in 1965 and in an 18-hole playoff in 1966. 
    Nick Faldo (1989–1990): Won both consecutive titles in playoffs, defeating Scott Hoch in 1989 and Raymond Floyd in 1990. 
    Tiger Woods (2001–2002): The most recent player to win back-to-back, securing his second and third green jackets. 
    Several players have won multiple Masters, but only these three have achieved it in consecutive years.

    Has anyone won back to back Masters?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Yes, three golfers have won the Masters back-to-back in its history: Jack Nicklaus (1965–66), Nick Faldo (1989–90), and Tiger Woods (2001–02). No player has achieved this feat in over two decades since Woods last accomplished it. 
    Back-to-Back Masters Winners: 
    Jack Nicklaus: Became the first to repeat, winning his second and third green jackets in consecutive years. 
    Nick Faldo: Won his second and third titles back-to-back, both in playoffs. 
    Tiger Woods: Won in 2001 and 2002 to join this elite group. 
    While many have tried to defend their title at Augusta National, only these three have successfully done so, making it one of the rarest achievements in golf.
